PHYSICS · LAUREATE 01

NEUTRINO ASTRONOMY · ICECUBE

FrancisHalzen.

A theoretical physicist and IceCube principal investigator who helped turn a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope for high-energy neutrinos.

Start the study lensPhysics overview
ROLEParticle astrophysicist
OBSERVATORYIceCube at the South Pole
BRIDGEAMANDA proof of concept → IceCube

WHY HE MATTERS

Make the invisible observable

Neutrinos interact so weakly that enormous detectors are needed to catch them. Halzen’s long leadership from AMANDA to IceCube helped make neutrino astronomy practical, opening a new way to study violent cosmic accelerators.

I
INPUT

A high-energy neutrino

A cosmic messenger passes through Earth and occasionally interacts near the detector.

P
PROCESS

Cherenkov light in clear ice

Thousands of optical sensors record the faint light pattern from secondary particles.

O
OUTPUT

Energy and arrival direction

Reconstruction points back toward candidate sources in the universe.

THREE-PASS REVIEW

Read the contribution from three angles

ACTIVE LENS

The person

Halzen is a theorist working across particle physics, astrophysics and cosmology. Since 1987, he pursued the South Pole detector concept from AMANDA to IceCube.
